q: Which strait near the tip of South America is named after a Portuguese explorer?
e: Named after Ferdinand Magellan, the strait cuts through southern Chile and links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

q: What is the capital of Finland?
e: Helsinki is the capital and largest city of Finland, located on the southern coast of the country by the Gulf of Finland.

q: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
e: Mandarin Chinese is the most spoken language by number of native speakers (about 920 million).

q: What is the name of the sea between Greece and Turkey?
e: The Aegean Sea is part of the Mediterranean, bounded by Greece to the west and north and Turkey to the east.

q: Which sea is surrounded by Turkey, Romania, Ukraine, and Russia?
e: The Black Sea is bordered by Turkey, Romania, Bulgaria, Ukraine, Russia, and Georgia.

q: What is the outermost layer of human skin called?
e: The epidermis is the outermost layer of skin. The dermis and the hypodermis sit beneath it.

q: What is the name of the brain region responsible for balance and coordination?
e: The cerebellum is the part of the brain located at the back and bottom, responsible for coordinating movement, balance, and posture.

q: What is the phenomenon when light bends around obstacles?
e: Diffraction is the bending of waves around obstacles or through openings, observed with light, sound, and water waves.

q: What is the name of the force that causes objects to resist changes in their motion?
e: Inertia is the tendency of an object to remain in its current state of motion unless acted upon by an external force (Newton's First Law).

q: What is the scientific name for the human species?
e: Modern humans belong to the species Homo sapiens, which means 'wise man' in Latin.

q: Which NFL team plays its home games at U.S. Bank Stadium?
e: U.S. Bank Stadium in downtown Minneapolis has been the Vikings' home since 2016.

q: Before moving to Indianapolis in 1984, the Colts played in which city?
e: The Colts moved from Baltimore to Indianapolis in March 1984.

q: Which MLB team plays its home games at Target Field?
e: Target Field in downtown Minneapolis has been the Twins' home since 2010.

q: Which NBA team plays its home games at the Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse?
e: Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse in downtown Cleveland is the home arena of the Cavaliers.

q: Which runner won the women's marathon at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics?
e: Kenya's Peres Jepchirchir won gold in the Tokyo Olympics marathon, which was run in Sapporo in 2021.

q: What film features Clarice Starling as an FBI trainee?
e: Clarice Starling is the protagonist of The Silence of the Lambs (1991), played by Jodie Foster.

q: Which TV show follows the Dutton family and their Montana ranch?
e: Yellowstone (2018–2024) follows John Dutton (Kevin Costner) and his family as they fight to keep their Montana ranch.

q: What is the name of the coffee shop in Friends?
e: Central Perk is the fictional coffeehouse in New York City where the Friends characters frequently hang out.

q: Who voices Elsa in Disney's 'Frozen'?
e: Idina Menzel voiced Queen Elsa in Frozen (2013), including the iconic song 'Let It Go'.

q: What is the name of the theme park island in Jurassic World?
e: Both the original Jurassic Park and Jurassic World are set on Isla Nublar.

q: What was the name of the British queen who ruled for 63 years in the 1800s?
e: Queen Victoria reigned from 1837 to 1901, the second-longest reign in British history, giving her name to the Victorian Era.

q: The English Civil War was fought mainly between which two sides?

e: Parliamentarians, or Roundheads, fought Royalists loyal to King Charles I from 1642 to 1651.

q: The Cultural Revolution in China was launched by which leader?
e: Mao Zedong launched the Cultural Revolution in 1966 to reassert communist ideology and eliminate political rivals.

q: Which medieval Islamic scholar is considered the father of sociology?
e: Ibn Khaldun (1332–1406) wrote the Muqaddimah, pioneering the study of social cohesion and historical analysis.

q: Who built the Taj Mahal?
e: Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, completed in 1643.

q: What is the name of the walking banana character in Fortnite?
e: Peely, the walking banana, has been one of Fortnite's best-known skins since 2019.

q: What is the highest rank in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive?
e: Global Elite is the highest competitive rank in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive.

q: What Nintendo franchise features kart racing with items?
e: Mario Kart launched in 1992 on SNES and remains Nintendo's most popular multiplayer racing franchise.

q: Who is the final boss of Diablo II: Lord of Destruction?
e: Baal, the Lord of Destruction, is the final boss of Act V, the act the expansion added.

q: What is the best hand in poker?
e: A Royal Flush is the best hand in standard poker, consisting of Ace, King, Queen, Jack, and Ten of the same suit.

q: What is the name of the first Beatles album released in the US?
e: Vee-Jay Records released Introducing... The Beatles in January 1964, ten days before Capitol's Meet the Beatles!

q: What is the name of the music term for a note that is held for its full length?
e: Tenuto indicates a note should be held for its full value, often with slight emphasis.

q: Which artist released 'Bad' and 'Billie Jean'?
e: Both 'Bad' (1987) and 'Billie Jean' (1982) are iconic Michael Jackson singles from his best-selling albums.

q: Les Paul is best known for pioneering which instrument?
e: Les Paul built one of the first solid-body electric guitars, nicknamed 'the Log,' around 1941. Gibson's Les Paul model is named after him.

q: Who released 'Shape of You' which became a massive global hit?
e: Ed Sheeran's 'Shape of You' from his 2017 album '÷' became one of the best-selling singles of all time.

q: Which currency is the official money of Vietnam?
e: The dong is the official currency of Vietnam.

q: Which currency is the official money of India?
e: The rupee is the official currency of India.

q: Which planet has an orbital period of about 29 Earth years?
e: Saturn takes about 29 Earth years to complete one orbit, so its seasons last for decades.

q: Which scientific law states that voltage equals current times resistance?
e: Ohm's law, named after Georg Ohm, says voltage equals current times resistance (V = IR).

q: The Pulitzer Prize is administered by which American university?
e: Columbia University in New York City has administered the Pulitzer Prize since 1917, as Joseph Pulitzer asked in his will.

q: Who plays Thor in the Marvel Cinematic Universe?
e: Australian actor Chris Hemsworth has portrayed Thor, the Asgardian god of thunder, across multiple MCU films since 'Thor' in 2011.

q: Who played Star-Lord in the 'Guardians of the Galaxy' movies?
e: Chris Pratt plays Peter Quill, aka Star-Lord, the half-human, half-alien leader of the Guardians of the Galaxy across multiple MCU films.

q: Who plays the Joker in the 2019 standalone film 'Joker'?
e: Joaquin Phoenix portrayed Arthur Fleck/Joker in the 2019 film directed by Todd Phillips, a performance that earned him the Academy Award for Best Actor.

q: What is the name of the famous meme featuring a dog sitting in a burning room?
e: The 'This is Fine' meme features a dog calmly sipping coffee while its house burns, created by KC Green in 2013.

q: Who played the title character in the 2023 film 'Oppenheimer'?
e: Irish actor Cillian Murphy played J. Robert Oppenheimer and won the Academy Award for Best Actor for the role.
